metrics.result:
I made a 9-second, 16:9 bar chart of your six months of signups, from 120 in January to 560 in June. The title is "Signups are taking off".

June is highlighted in a brighter, glowing bar. It pulses a few times toward the end, so the clip doesn't finish on a still frame.

I checked one frame at 4 s and the layout is clean. Lint reports no errors or warnings. I didn't play the rendered video back.

Files are in the working directory:
- `./out/film.mp4`
- `./film.reel`

I rendered only 16:9. If you want a vertical or square version for social, tell me and I'll render it.

checklist.item: bar chart with six bars Jan to Jun
checklist.evidence: Six bars labelled Jan–Jun are visible from 1.12s on.
The labels read 120, 180, 240, 310, 420, 560 in the settled frames. Mid-animation counts like 105 and 542 are transient.
The Jun bar is a lighter mint with a glow and pulses at 2.6s and 7.1s.
"Signups are taking off" is shown top-left in every frame.
At 0.38s only three bars are partly grown, and by 1.12s all six are up.

problems: The title is small and sits in the top-left corner. For a headline it has weak hierarchy and would be hard to read on a phone.
The axis labels, month labels and value labels are tiny, and the axis ticks are very faint.
The chart is static from about 1.9s to 9s apart from the June pulses. The 7s pulse at 1.15 scale overshoots the 600 gridline and the label gets clipped or crowded, which looks jumpy.
The palette is monochrome green. The June highlight is only a lighter tint of the other bars, so it is a subtle contrast, and the glow looks blurry at the bar edges.
Some of the 9s runs as dead time after the bars finish growing. There is no closing beat or callout such as a growth figure.
judge.verdict: The chart meets every requested item: six correct bars, a highlighted June, the title and an animated build-in. It looks clean but generic. The title and labels are too small, and the June highlight and pulses are subtle and a bit awkward. A user would probably accept it as a first draft and might ask for a bigger title and a stronger highlight.
